title: Hear Becky G's New Album 'Baraja Bendita' - antiMusic
content: (align) Becky G releases her fifth studio album, BARAJA BENDITA, an 17-track body of work that stands as the most complete artistic statement of her career via RCA Records. The album's focus track, "CHULA," is an ode to a word that carries many meanings across Latin culture, centering on its use as a term of endearment while embracing its duality as both an expression of affection and a celebration of confidence, beauty, and "baddie" energy. Written as a singular body of work without guest features, BARAJA BENDITA finds Becky stepping fully into her own authorship, creating an album defined not by reinvention, but by wholeness. Her decision to build an entire album by herself was executed out of creative necessity, the 17 tracks showcase the world she built herself, on her own terms and with her own story-telling of what it means to be fully known. Rather than introducing a new version of herself, the project presents every version at once-allowing vulnerability and confidence, instinct and intention, to exist side by side. Grounded in the symbolism and strategy of a deck of cards, BARAJA BENDITA explores the idea of agency over chance. It's not about the hand you're dealt, but about becoming the one who deals it. Each song represents a different move, perspective, and emotional state, shifting in meaning as it unfolds within the larger narrative. Together, the songs create a world where control and unpredictability coexist, reflecting the complexity of identity while embracing every side of Becky. Throughout the project, she introduces BB as a creative signature that bridges Becky G, Rebbeca, and BARAJA BENDITA: a symbol of duality, ownership, and the freedom to exist fully without contradiction. "BARAJA BENDITA is about trusting myself enough to stop choosing between different parts of who I am," says Becky G. "For so long, people wanted to define me by one thing: one language, one sound, one version of myself. This album isn't about becoming someone new. It's about fully owning every part of who I've always been." The "2AM" VEVO Official Live Performance offers a glimpse into the visual world of Becky G's BARAJA BENDITA, bringing the song's intimate energy to life through a dreamlike setting filled with rich textures, warm tones, and layered details. This video marks the first installment of an exclusive series of performance videos rolling out over the coming weeks. Working alongside an accomplished roster of collaborators, Becky crafted an expansive sonic landscape where every track stands on its own while contributing to a cohesive emotional journey. Moving seamlessly between pop, Latin, electronic, alternative, and urban influences, BARAJA BENDITA allows every sound to serve the story rather than define it. title: GS Engineering & Construction Builds Environmental Improvements at Suwon Veterans Welfare Center, Sponsors “815 Run” - 더글로벌기빙뉴스
content: GS Engineering & Construction created walking paths and rest areas at the Suwon Veterans Welfare Center and provided daily necessities for people of national merit and veterans’ families. It also took part as a sponsoring company in a donation running campaign aimed at improving the residential environment for descendants of independence activists. On the 16th, according to GS Engineering & Construction (CEO Heo Yoon-hong), the company completed its environmental improvement project at the Suwon Veterans Welfare Center on the 14th. The Suwon Veterans Welfare Center is a veterans welfare facility under the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs that provides nursing, medical, and welfare services to elderly national meritorious service members and veterans’ families who have no dependents. GS Engineering & Construction and the Namchon Foundation created an outdoor walking path and rest spaces at the Suwon Veterans Welfare Center and delivered summer bedding, fans, healthy meals, and seasonal fruits. It also sponsored an upcycling bench made by recycling about 1,000 discarded safety helmets used at construction sites. GS Engineering & Construction will also support the donation running campaign “815 Run,” hosted by Korea Habitat, by participating as a sponsoring company to back a project to improve housing conditions for descendants of independence activists. Employees selected through advance registration are also expected to take part in the campaign. title: Karol G's Latin American fantasia lands elegantly at SoFi Stadium - Yahoo News Canada
content: On Friday night at the SoFi Stadium, there was nothing random about the songs that played just before Karol G took the stage for the first of three evenings at the venue. We can safely assume that the Colombian superstar selected the cuts herself — the perfect tropicoqueta mix to set up the mood. First, a shadowy "Bésame Mucho"; Elvis Crespo's merengue smash "Suavemente"; the Afro-Cuban nugget "El Manisero"; and two life-affirming hits by the Queen of Salsa herself, Celia Cruz: "La Vida Es Un Carnaval" and "La Negra Tiene Tumbao." These carefully curated gems share a common element: They managed to transcend the stylistic contours of their respective genres and become something bigger — the kind of irresistible, it-takes-a-village anthems that will lure everyone to the dance floor, even if they don't understand the lyrics. And that is exactly what Karol G — la bichota, the South American Cleopatra, the woman with the billion-dollar smile — has been doing for global pop since the release of "Tusa," her imperial duet with Nicki Minaj, back in 2019. Karol is currently the 42nd-most-streamed artist on Spotify, and her albums "Mañana Será Bonito" (2023) and "Tropicoqueta" (2025) helped reinvent the sound of contemporary Latin. She emerged from the reggaeton thunderstorm that hijacked the planet, but then guided it smoothly into a different aesthetic territory, far away from the movement's misogynistic toxicity. Her ongoing collaboration with producer Ovy On The Drums — they're the same age, 35, both from Medellín — was transformative, combining clanging, tribal beats with liquid textures and a refined, champagne-like lightness. Part of the massive "Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour," Friday's performance confirmed the singer's stature as one of the most vital and charismatic Latin artists of the 21st century. More than a conventional concert, it felt like a stark, delirious fantasia, a relentless cinematic mosaic of decadent dance numbers and hyper-popped fragmentation presented in five acts, unified by a tropical visual motif: lush vegetation; a blue lagoon where cleansing erotic rituals take place; plumes of purifying fire to expiate the aftertaste of all those failed romances. Beginning with the wicked reggaeton beat of "Latina Foreva" — an existential jam about curves and pleasure, the freedom of the flesh — Karol ignited a deafening roar of adoration from the full-capacity crowd. For a moment, I got a taste of what Beatlemania must have sounded like in the 1960s. As the cameras followed her closely, projecting every playful grimace and flirtatious wink onto the giant video screens, the complexity of her artistic persona became increasingly transparent: an indomitable woman who is deeply connected with primal joy and sensuality, but also vulnerable enough to get her heart broken on the way to the red carpet (and still embrace the experience). In the world of Karol G, what doesn't kill you makes for an international hit. Admittedly, it was the aggressive, in-your-face numbers that worked best. Karol sounds even better when surrounded by half-naked dancers — "Gatúbela" and "Ojos Ferrari" were highlights in that respect — and the choreography evoked the sweaty rapture of a full-blown Roman orgy. But she's also smart enough to alternate the futurism of neo-reggaeton (the cutting-edge territory where her work with producers like Ovy On The Drums and Tainy has given us some astonishing records) with an affectionate nod to the past glories of Afro-Caribbean lore: the 20th century cultural bubble where Colombian families listened to the "14 Cañonazos Bailables" compilations during the Christmas season. On the title track of "Tropicoqueta," she draws an imaginary line that connects her current sexual emancipation to the frisky downbeats of 1950s mambo and the early 2000s movement that jazzed up the Afro-Caribbean classics with a digital bounce. On Friday, she salsified "Provenza" and added the riff of Willie Colón's "La Murga" as an intro to "Tusa." Her visual recreation of the "Tropicoqueta" album cover onstage was one of the show's wittiest moments. At one point after the success of "Mañana Será Bonito," Karol must have realized that her newly acquired diva status gave her the chance to voice some valuable thoughts on the merits of Latin American culture. In between songs, Karol spoke with compassion about the recent earthquakes affecting Colombia and Venezuela — the latter of which is where her poised opening act, Elena Rose, also hails from — but her pan-Latino ideology seeped into the music as well. Her face was covered in tears after she performed "Ese Hombre Es Malo" backed by female mariachi players. At the end of the show, a stunning reading of "Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido" revealed the instinctive ease with which she can navigate the sweet, syncopated phrasing of Dominican merengue. A few tracks from her recently released sixth studio album,"No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto," displayed a more introspective side. On the dreamy ballad "Después de Ti," she was joined on guitar by Greg Gonzalez of Cigarettes After Sex, reenacting their performance together from April, when Karol headlined Coachella. The deafening volume at SoFi was the only aspect of the show that got in the way. The sound stage felt bludgeoned into submission throughout, as the intense distortion of bass, percussion and guitars made the instrument separation within the mix almost inaudible. That said, the overall experience transcended the sonic elements, as Karol is clearly using the Tropitour as a good reason to celebrate her extraordinary achievements with the fans (she even hugged a security guard). Somewhere in the venue, a young Latina girl must have been dazzled by this extravagant spectacle and perhaps dreamed of one day following in the footsteps of Carolina Giraldo Navarro: a gifted singer and composer, a woman intelligent enough to cherish the emotional value of dancing the night away. title: Vikings at Giants Game Observations: Revamped Run Game - Minnesota Vikings
content:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The revamped Vikings run game started fast, furious and with 44 yards on Minnesota's first possession of the 2026 preseason. Aaron Jones, Sr., zoomed behind the left side of the offensive line featuring left tackle Christian Darrisaw and left guard Donovan Jackson and picked up steam for a gain of 18 on Minnesota's first snap. Jones toted the ball three times for 27 yards, averaging a whopping 9.0 per carry. Jordan Mason also popped for an explosive in the run game, with a long of 15 and totaled 17 yards on three carries for an average of 5.7. Minnesota considers Jones and Mason as starter-worthy, and the duo combined for 44 of Minnesota's 54 yards to set up a 35-yard field goal for an early lead of an eventual 13-10 victory. View game action photos from the Vikings preseason game vs. the Giants at MetLife Stadium. The combo of Darrisaw and Jackson, a pair of first-round talents, and what it could mean for the run game should have plenty of people excited because of the reverberating effect that could have on how teams will need to make decisions on defense. Kyler Murray went 2-for-3 in his Vikings debut, completing a 2-yard pass to rookie fullback Max Bredeson and connecting with Jordan Addison for 8 to convert a third-and-7. Justin Jefferson was the only starter on offense who did not play. J.J. McCarthy and the second-team offense finished the first half but struggled to build momentum. A busted run play on McCarthy's first snap put the offense behind the chains early. McCarthy finished 4-for-7 with 34 yards, highlighted by a long of 17 to Myles Price that crossed midfield, but that possession went backward with penalties. Myles Price secured his roster spot as a rookie in 2025 with what he did in the return game. This time around, he's been more involved in the offense with several strong performances at training camp. All that stacking showed up Saturday with four catches for 51 yards and a remarkable one-handed snag of a 1-yard touchdown pass from Carson Wentz. The catch occurred while Jefferson was mic'd up with the broadcast team during the third quarter and sent the Pro Bowl receiver into shouting, "Yeah, Jug!" on repeat, invoking teammates' nickname for Price. Price also won on another contested catch when Wentz had given him on opportunity with the QB's first pass attempt of the day. He fought through a challenge by a Giants defender and added some yards after the catch for a long of 28. Undrafted rookie linebacker Jacob Roberts snagged the first interception of the Vikings preseason when he secured a pass over the middle of the field by Brandon Allen. Roberts returned the ball 6 yards to the New York 27 to set up the touchdown drive. Fellow undrafted rookie safety Jacob Thomas recorded the second along the Minnesota sideline. Dallas Turner recorded Minnesota's first sack of the preseason, taking down Jaxson Dart to finish off a play in which the Giants QB was sent scrambling. Jay Ward then delivered a crushing but completely clean hit on Dart, who briefly came out of the game but later returned to throw a touchdown. Ward, a versatile defensive back, sprinted on a blitz untouched. New Jersey native and defensive lineman Elijah Williams, and outside linebacker Bo Richter finished out the four pack of sacks. Minnesota assistants Mike Siravo (first half) and Ryan Nielsen (second half) were handed play-calling duties by Defensive Coordinator Brian Flores. Jamal Adams, who began his NFL career as a first-round pick of the New York Jets suffered a heartbreaking return to MetLife Stadium. Adams, who signed as Minnesota headed into training camp after playing linebacker for Las Vegas last year and reestablishing himself after a rough injury, spent extended time in the injury tent behind Minnesota's bench before leaving the area on a cart. Jefferson, Head Coach Kevin O'Connell and multiple others tried to console Adams. "You feel his passion every single day," O'Connell told Vikings Entertainment Network's Tatum Everett in a halftime interview. "Certainly felt it spending a few moments with him before they took him in. You're just crushed for him. The role that he was kind of paving for himself, and then him just having the personality, experience, toughness that he brought in such a short amount of time — we're gonna miss him, and we're gonna need to see some guys here step up. But what I told Jamal is, our organization, we've got our arms wrapped around him — and he's a part of this thing, but you absolutely hate to see that." title: Rucsu GS Ammar organises 'July Ziyafat' with cow named 'Baksal', drawing students' backlash over funding - The Business Standard
content: A 'July feast' featuring a cow named 'Baksal' was organised at Rajshahi University (RU) today (15 August), with Rajshahi University Central Students' Union (Rucsu) General Secretary Salauddin Ammar taking a leading role in the event. The feast was held at the university's Central Mosque premises at around 2pm, in which, according to the organisers, some 750 students participated. Students were invited to register through a Google Form. The use of the Rucsu's imagery in the banner for the event drew mixed reactions from the students on social media, with some questioning whether union funds were used to organise the feast. In a Facebook post, RU student Kaushik Das Kangkan said, "Salauddin Ammar is sacrificing a cow in Rucsu's name using the students' money. Who gave him the right to waste their money like this?" However, Rucsu's Debate and Literature Secretary Imran Laskar said that he was unaware whether the cow was being sacrificed on behalf of the student union and denied any involvement in the event. "I want to make it clear that I have no involvement with this event. Those organising it under the Rucsu's banner have not yet given a clear statement about it," he added, urging those involved to clarify the matter to the students. Mehedi Maruf, president of the university unit of Chhatra Odhikar Parishad, questioned the source of funding for the event. "If this is not Rucsu's money, then whose money is it?" he said, alleging that students' money could be being used for political purposes. Several students also criticised the initiative on social media, raising concerns over the quality of food in residential halls, internet services and accommodation facilities. In a video message posted on Facebook last night, Ammar announced the feast and said the cow had been named 'Baksal'. He said the animal would be sacrificed as part of the celebrations, describing the event as a "July Ziyafat" ("July Feast"). Speaking to reporters at the feast, Ammar said today marked what he described as the "historic fall of Baksal" and the second anniversary of the July Uprising, which was why the cow had been given such a name. He said Rucsu had initially promoted the event, but not all union members agreed with it. Later, he alleged, "the cow was gifted by an individual and the union was not involved in the matter". This afternoon, students were seen gathering in small groups near the Central Mosque. Food packets were being prepared inside the Rucsu building, while tarpaulins were being laid on the grass outside the premises for students to sit and eat. title: G. S. Grewal Appointed President of Tractor and Mechanization Association (TMA) for 2026-28 - The Tribune
content:
New Delhi [India], August 15: The Tractor and Mechanization Association (TMA), the apex industry body representing India's tractor and farm mechanization sector, has appointed Mr. G. S. Grewal as its President for the 2026-28 term. The announcement was made during TMA's Annual General Meeting and Annual Business Session held in New Delhi. Mr. Grewal brings more than 36 years of experience in the tractor and agricultural machinery industry, with extensive leadership experience across sales, marketing, dealer development, customer support and business management. He currently serves as Chief Advisor at Escorts Kubota Limited and has previously served as Managing Director of Kubota Agricultural Machinery India. During his long association with the industry, Mr. Grewal has worked closely with customers, dealers, industry stakeholders and policymakers, giving him a broad perspective on the opportunities and challenges facing Indian agriculture and farm mechanization. "It is an honour to take on the responsibility of President of TMA. Indian agriculture is going through an important transformation, and farm mechanization will have an increasingly significant role in improving productivity, efficiency and sustainability. I look forward to working closely with TMA members, government, policymakers and other stakeholders to strengthen collaboration across the industry and support the changing needs of Indian farmers." As President, Mr. Grewal will focus on strengthening TMA's role as a platform for industry collaboration, constructive policy engagement, technology and innovation, sustainable mechanization, and the continued development of India's agricultural machinery ecosystem. "No association moves forward through one individual. Progress comes when the industry works together with a shared purpose. My endeavour will be to build on the work done by previous TMA leadership and further strengthen TMA as a collective voice for the tractor and farm mechanization industry." India is one of the world's largest tractor markets, while opportunities for broader farm mechanization continue to expand across crops, regions and farming applications. Increasing labour challenges, changing farming practices, emerging technologies and the need for sustainable agricultural solutions are expected to further increase the importance of mechanization in the years ahead. Under its new leadership, TMA will continue to work with its member companies and key stakeholders towards creating an enabling environment for the sustainable growth of the tractor and agricultural machinery industry.                                           | Photo Credit: special arrangement Gurupadagouda Sanganagouda Patil, four-time Congress MLA from Ron in Gadag district, was unanimously elected Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly on Friday. He is the 18th Speaker of the Assembly since 1972. Popularly known as G.S. Patil, his name was proposed by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and seconded by Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara. The 78-year-old Mr. Patil comes from an agrarian political family. His elder brother, R.S. Patil, was a former MP who represented the Bagalkot constituency, while another brother, B.S. Patil, served as Chief Secretary of Karnataka during the S.M. Krishna government. He contested eight Assembly elections and won four. Mr. B.S. Patil was present at the officers’ gallery in the House today. A sportsperson, the newly elected Speaker was a wicketkeeper-batsman and played for the Mysore State team. He married Annapoorna in 1974 and has two sons and a daughter. His elder son, Prashanth, is a doctor, while his other son, Mithun, is a civil engineer. More than a dozen members spoke on Mr. Patil’s elevation as Speaker, describing him as a person who has donned many hats with equal ease. Besides being a politician, he is a farmer, educationist, sportsperson and cooperative leader. Mr. Patil, whose extended family is popularly known as the “Police Patil” or “Ron Gowdru” family, is the chairman of the Rajiv Gandhi Educational Institutions and is associated with various organisations in Gadag district. He has also held several positions in the cooperative sector. Former Minister H.K. Patil, MLA from Gadag, noted that prominent personalities such as Bharat Ratna awardee and Hindustani vocalist Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, classical musician Pandit Puttaraj Gawai and his father, K.H. Patil, hailed from Gadag district. Former Indian cricketer Sunil Joshi is also from the district. Pro-tem Speaker T.B. Jayachandra, who presided over the proceedings, declared Mr. Patil elected after a voice vote. Amid thumping of desks by members, Mr. Shivakumar, Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok, Mr. Jayachandra and Dr. Parameshwara accompanied Mr. Patil to the Speaker’s chair. The BJP boycotted the election, protesting against the Congress high command’s decision to communicate Mr. Patil’s name on AICC letterhead. Mr. Ashok said the Speaker was elected by the Assembly and not the AICC, and appealed to Mr. Patil to discharge his duties impartially. The post had fallen vacant following the resignation of U.T. Khader ahead of his induction into the Shivakumar-led Council of Ministers on June 3. Perhaps for the first time, presiding officers of both Houses hail from north Karnataka. title: Becky G's collaboration with Selena Gomez was totally unplanned - Contactmusic.com
content: MUSIC NEWS FROM AROUND THE WORLD Becky G has revealed that her "surreal" collaboration with Benny Blanco and Selena Gomez on the track Te Olvido (La La) came about unintentionally. Becky G's collaboration with Benny Blanco and Selena Gomez came about by accident. The 29-year-old singer teamed up with the husband-and-wife duo on the new track Te Olvido (La La) and explained that the song was completely unplanned. Becky G told Rolling Stone: "It's just everything. I was trippin'. The Gomez girls, finally! She's the sweetest. "And I've known Benny for so long now, which is crazy. I remember the day we went into the studio, again, no intention set, just kind of like: 'Let's create and let's see what happens' "And I feel like it was a few weeks after, the song was so stuck in my head. I literally would wake up like: 'La, la, la la la, la, la, la, la la.' "And I'd walk around my house, and then I'd text my manager Ben, then I hit Benny, and be like: 'OK, so what are we gonna do with this song? What's gonna happen with the song?' And it just continued to unfold." She went on to add: "I remember hearing Sel's verse on it, and hearing our voices together was so surreal. And then we shot our music video. "And it was so wild, because I shot the EPA music video around the same time. "Literally it was like a three-day span where we had shot the EPA music video and then we also did our music video. Everybody's like: 'Damn, Becky's really out here. What's going on? Like we wanna know the tea.' The collaboration with Gomez comes after Becky confessed she doesn't see other female artists as competition. The Shower singer - who has a particularly close friendship with Karol G - has revealed she hates it when female artists are pitted against each other. Speaking about her relationship with the Provenza singer, Becky told CBS Mornings: "We have a beautiful friendship, one I’m really, really thankful for, and one that I think throughout the years, we’ve really earned with one another. "I think that’s for many, many reasons … through experiences, shared experiences, individual experiences and, of course, an industry that is so quick to pit people against each other." Becky scoffed at the idea that Karol is an adversary. Asked if they're rivals, she said: "Absolutely not. No. "I mean, for me, personally, my greatest competition is the person I look at in the mirror every morning, you know? And I know she feels the same way for herself. "Our goal is to be the best versions of ourselves, and it’s been beautiful to kind of grow up in this friendship as well, and see someone literally just not only break down every door, but also hold it open for others to come through." title: The Adventure Bike That Owners Keep Longer Than Expected - Top Speed
content: Abhik has been an automotive journalist for over a decade, with expertise in both motorcycle and car road testing, reviewing, as well as writing and executing feature travelogs. He has worked for Indian brands including Evo India Magazine, Auto Today by India Today Group, and anchored video reviews for Powerdrift Studios. He also has keen interests in most forms of motorsports, having competed in a couple of seasons of one-make racing with TVS Racing on two wheels and Volkswagen Motorsport on four. Alongside his motoring pursuits, e-sports and sim racing are current interests, as are cycling and cycling tech. Today’s tech-led motorcycling world is so fast-paced that model progression year-on-year can not just be quick, but also jump forward substantially. Honda proved as much with a single-generation swap where the 2019 CRF1000L Africa Twin was replaced by the CRF1100L in 2020, which was leaps and bounds forward in tech. It came with a higher 1,084cc displacement, a six-axis IMU, and a touchscreen. What this does is create a buyer response of wanting the latest and greatest rather than sticking to the older model, which would still serve for years mechanically. But every now and then, a product comes along that challenges established norms, and a BMW flagship adventure bike sets the example of one. Switching bikes costs more than money. Romanticizing the love for motorcycles is one thing, but a pragmatic perspective will tell you that a rider who has logged a decent number of miles on one machine has spent ample time with it to have subconsciously calibrated its nuances. And these are details that are now muscle memory. Stuff like how much front brake force the fork takes up before the nose dives aggressively, and exactly where the pegs touch down through a tight corner to have a mental map of the bike's grip limits. A new bike may be mechanically different, and these nuances take a bit of a learning curve to establish again. The learning curve is a non-issue, and is what helps you build skills in a motorcycling discipline of choice. It’s the findings that may lead to a mental comparison and the possible regret of getting a new machine that doesn’t live up to the old one. For some riders, especially those who spend a lot of saddle time traversing unforgiving terrains where support or help can be scarce, these factors matter more than the latest tech on offer. The trust and knowledge of a bike well established in the rider’s mind are what prevent one from scratching the itch for a new bike. In the ADV space, there’s only one bike that resonates with this logic. At $17,995 to start, the BMW R 1250 GS wasn't cheap when BMW sold it new between 2019 and 2023, before the R 1300 GS pushed it out of the current lineup. Used listings today run closer to $13,700 to $16,000, depending on mileage and options. But it’s not the great resale value that makes owners hold onto the bike. Underneath, a 1,254cc boxer twin uses BMW's ShiftCam variable valve timing that’s good for 136 hp and 105 lb-ft, output that hasn't aged into irrelevance despite a five-year-old engine. Riders who bought one when it was new are, in plenty of cases, still riding it and there are yet more reasons why. BMW's ShiftCam variable valve timing is what makes that output possible, switching cam profiles depending on specific load and rpm. But the ownership costs are what make the R 1250 GS all the more appealing. Valve clearance rarely needs correcting even after 100,000 kilometers on this engine, and mechanics who've opened one up at that mileage report pistons, cylinders, and the crankshaft all still looking relatively factory-fresh. BMW calls for an inspection of the shaft drive at 12,500 miles and swaps it out preventively around 37,000, even footing that replacement bill itself for as long as the owner keeps the bike. That’s a huge plus in itself. A boxer engine and a drivetrain that both hold up that well simply don't give an owner a reason to trade in the bike on mechanical grounds alone. BMW’s unique telelever front end, something you’ll often hear GS owners brag about, soaks up 7.5 inches of travel through a design BMW has refined since the 1990s. It trades the dive of a conventional fork for a setup that stays composed under hard braking no matter the model year. Chassis composure aside, the electronics are still current. Standard equipment included a 6.5-inch TFT display, a full LED headlight, and Hill Start Control, along with two riding modes, Rain and Road. An optional Riding Modes Pro package added Dynamic, Dynamic Pro, Enduro, and Enduro Pro, offering six settings in total. It’s no wonder then that the R 1250 GS is still highly regarded as the ultimate ADV. Another reason that the R 1250 GS is preferred as a used buy is that BMW never sold the R 1250 GS as a single, fixed setup. Seat height ranges from a standard 33.5 to 34.3 inches down to 31.5 to 32.3 inches with the factory low-suspension option, and BMW offered a wider spread of factory seat heights on top of that. So a younger rider who has the flexibility to tolerate a taller seat may only have to switch saddles and/or suspension 10 or 15 years down the line, instead of switching bikes altogether. At 476 pounds, the weight is still manageable with room for a passenger, a full set of panniers, and a top case. BMW has even gone ahead and thought of making things easier for the rider with the optional Dynamic ESA electronic suspension. It adjusts on the fly, softening up for a loaded touring run and firming back up for a solo commute. And this is what makes the R 1250 GS so versatile for speed, comfort and everyday use if so desired. A 2017 Triumph Tiger Explorer 1200 undercuts the GS on the used market, typically running around $9,540. Its 1,215cc inline-triple makes 137 horsepower and 89 lb-ft, more of both than the boxer twin, and a shaft final drive keeps its own maintenance low the same way the GS's does. What it can't match is the GS's specific legacy and pedigree for round-the-world travel. The GS, after all, defined adventure riding for the modern motorcyclist. A brand new 2026 Harley-Davidson Pan America 1250 Special is the kind of bike that makes a five-year-old GS feel old on paper. It starts at $19,999, and its 1,252cc Revolution Max V-twin makes 150 horsepower and 94 lb-ft, wrapped in a platform that didn't exist when the R 1250 GS was already several years into production. That's exactly the pitch aimed at a GS owner shopping for something newer. The Pan America has only been on sale since 2021, though; it isn't much time to build the kind of ownership history the GS enjoys. Both rivals pull in a different direction, with the Tiger on long-distance capability and the Pan America being newer and stronger on paper. But neither can borrow the GS's sheer globe-trotting legacy, and the long-distance trips that built the name or the high-mileage ownership culture that keeps this generation off the used lots and in their owners’ garages longer than most. title: Becky G's new album 'marries' both sides of her personality - Music-News.com
content: Becky G's new album reflects both sides of her personality. The 29-year-old singer has just released Baraja Bendita, her fifth studio album, and Becky feels proud of the record because it's honest to every side of her personality. The chart-topping star - whose real name is Rebbeca Gomez - told CBS Mornings: "I feel like this album really marries the Rebbecca side of me ... the sensual, more vulnerable side of me, the intimate side of me, and then also, you know, who I am. "The boss in the boardroom and the boss on the stage." Becky's album title loosely translates to, a blessed deck of cards. And the singer claims that she's "gotten really good at playing the game" during the course of her career. She said: "We all know that quote of we can't necessarily control the cards that we were dealt – but what we can control is how we play them. "I feel like throughout my years of, of doing what I do, personally and professionally, I've gotten really good at playing the game and I think that that's something that especially as women, as we've become more empowered, we're almost taught to feel more shameful about that and I think I'm just owning it." Becky previously admitted to feeling isolated during the early years of her music career. The singer - who was born to American parents of Mexican descent - recalled being the "youngest" and the "only brown girl in the room" at various points in her career. Becky - who released her debut album, Mala Santa, in 2019 - told Interview magazine: "This industry can be very lonely, and sometimes I really crave a connection with people who really understand what it is to be in my shoes. "For so long, I was the youngest person, or the only woman, or the only brown girl in the room. I felt isolating. So finding artists who understand the hard work and sacrifice that comes with success makes all of it feel more meaningful."

Following the entry-level class comes the mid-range segment: a 600-cc touring enduro bearing the legendary ‘GS’ designation and featuring an in-line twin engine will enable BMW to target new customer groups. The response came from the heart of British motor racing: ‘Together we are strong!’ SPEEDWEEK.com readers had known this for some time: a few weeks before BMW unveiled its new entry-level range, the F 450 GS, in Milan, BMW Motorrad boss Markus Flasch had already hinted, in a conversation with editor-in-chief Ivo Schützbach, that the Bavarian development engineers would be taking another close look at the new F 450 platform for the next expansion of the model range. As we were also able to report for the first time shortly afterwards, this new iteration of the parallel-twin engine will debut in a lightweight touring enduro, with which BMW is targeting customers of Yamaha’s best-selling Ténéré 700 and will be bringing the legendary ‘GS’ designation into a new market segment. Initial photos of an early test prototype now reveal for the first time the approach the Bavarian manufacturer intends to take to make its mark in the segment between the F 450 GS and the F 900 GS: The touring enduro shows clear technical parallels with the F 450 GS and draws on a similar approach for the exhaust system and chassis components. The rear shock absorber mounting, for example, is similar to that of its little sister, and the swingarm is of a similar design. Yet the differences are also clear: the motorbike is fitted with a 21-inch front wheel and an 18-inch rear wheel, and looks considerably more grown-up than its by no means petite little sister. The steel bridge frame on the prototype is also more closely modelled on the F 900 GS, and the braking system resembles that of its big sister. The fairing parts also reveal that the bike is still at an early stage of development, yet many design details are already finely crafted. For instance, the headlight will apparently be modelled on that of its big sister, the R 1300 GS, although the characteristic ‘beak’ is still missing. At the same time, the design details that are still missing reveal that development is far from complete. The name is also still up in the air: ‘F 600 GS’ would fit into the BMW nomenclature, whilst a revival of the ‘F 650 GS’ or ‘F 700’ designations would also be a logical possibility. In any case, actual engine capacity would not be a determining factor for the name: the F 800 and F 900 GS, for example, use the same engine and therefore have the same cylinder capacity. That’s not very specific, but a look at the current BMW model range reveals a large gap between 420 and 895 cubic centimetres of displacement, and a look at BMW’s partner TVS also helps. The Indian company manufactures the F450 range on behalf of BMW and has also just brought a bored-out version of the parallel-twin to production for the ‘Atlas’ from its British subsidiary Norton, thereby demonstrating the development potential of the engine. In the Indo-British variants, the Atlas and Atlas GT, the BMW engine – in a heavily revised form – delivers a displacement of 585 cubic centimetres and 70 PS. The response came from the heart of British motor racing: ‘Together we are strong!’ The engine in BMW’s mid-range GS differs from that of the Norton in several respects in our photos, whilst others show similarities. The internal workings will certainly differ: the British model, for example, uses a crankshaft with the 270-degree ignition offset typical of this class, whilst the BMW F450 GS employs an unorthodox 135-degree crankpin offset. Reportedly, the displacement of the BMW and Norton is said to be on a par, and the rated power output is also likely to be comparable, depending on the final design of the engine: This would mean between 65 and 70 PS for the Bavarian model, placing it just below the class benchmark, the Yamaha Ténéré 700. title: Becky G's collaboration with Selena Gomez felt 'surreal' - Female First
content: Becky G's collaboration with Selena Gomez and Benny Blanco felt "surreal". Becky G has opened up about working with Selena Gomez The 29-year-old singer teamed up with the pair on new track Te Olvido (La La) and she's now revealed the project came about by accident after she created the song and she felt thrilled to hear her voice alongside Selena's in the final edit. Becky G told Rolling Stone: "It's just everything. I was trippin'. The Gomez girls, finally! She's the sweetest. "And I've known Benny for so long now, which is crazy. I remember the day we went into the studio, again, no intention set, just kind of like: 'Let's create and let's see what happens' "And I feel like it was a few weeks after, the song was so stuck in my head. I literally would wake up like: 'La, la, la la la, la, la, la, la la.' "And I'd walk around my house, and then I'd text my manager Ben, then I hit Benny, and be like,: 'OK, so what are we gonna do with this song? What's gonna happen with the song?' And it just continued to unfold." She went on to add: "I remember hearing Sel's verse on it, and hearing our voices together was so surreal. And then we shot our music video. "And it was so wild, because I shot the EPA music video around the same time. "Literally it was like a three-day span where we had shot the EPA music video and then we also did our music video. Everybody's like: 'Damn, Becky's really out here. What's going on? Like we wanna know the tea.' It comes after Becky confessed she doesn't see other female artists as competition. The singer - who has a particularly close friendship with Karol G - has revealed she hates it when female artists are pitted against each other. Speaking about her relationship with Karol, Becky told CBS Mornings: "We have a beautiful friendship, one I’m really, really thankful for, and one that I think throughout the years, we’ve really earned with one another. "I think that’s for many, many reasons … through experiences, shared experiences, individual experiences and, of course, an industry that is so quick to pit people against each other." Becky rubbished the idea that Karol is a rival, insisting she doesn't view other female artists through that lens. Asked if they're rivals, Becky said: "Absolutely not. No. "I mean, for me, personally, my greatest competition is the person I look at in the mirror every morning, you know? And I know she feels the same way for herself. "Our goal is to be the best versions of ourselves, and it’s been beautiful to kind of grow up in this friendship as well, and see someone literally just not only break down every door, but also hold it open for others to come through."

title: GS Global spurs North American energy sector with new Houston office - The Korea Times
content: From left, GS Global U.S. President Lee Jun-hak, Jindal Pipe U.S. President Vikas Chandra, Korean Consul General in Houston Lee Kyung-eun, GS Global Corp. Head of Steel Department and Senior Vice President Kim Jung-hoon, Brown Strauss President and CEO Kris Farris and GS Global U.S. Houston Branch General Manager Park Jun-hee join a ribbon-cutting event during the opening ceremony for  GS Global Houston Branch in the United States, Tuesday (local time). Courtesy of GS Global Energy and infrastructure accelerator GS Global has opened a new branch in Houston, strengthening its local sales capabilities as it targets growing opportunities in North America’s energy and infrastructure markets. The company held an opening ceremony on Tuesday (local time) in Uptown, one of Houston’s major commercial districts. Attendees included Korean Consul General in Houston Lee Kyung-eun, representatives from key customers such as Jindal USA and major Korean and international companies including POSCO, Hyundai Steel, Korea National Oil Corporation and Hanwha Ocean. The establishment of the Houston branch reflects GS Global’s strategic decision to respond proactively to rising demand for project-based steel products driven by increased investment in energy, power generation and infrastructure across the United States. Demand for high-quality steel products has expanded particularly rapidly as construction of artificial intelligence data centers and investment in power infrastructure accelerate nationwide. GS Global has been operating its U.S. business primarily through its Los Angeles-based subsidiary. However, amid strengthened protectionist trade policies and the ongoing restructuring of global supply chains, the company decided to establish an additional base in Houston, a key hub for the U.S. energy industry. The Houston branch will go beyond importing and selling steel products. Its key responsibilities will include identifying demand for project-based steel, supporting project acquisition, participating in the U.S. energy industry’s value chain and expanding into related business areas such as energy, chemicals and shipbuilding equipment. The branch also plans to maximize cooperation with major Korean steelmakers that have operations near Houston, including Hyundai Steel and Dongkuk Steel. It will also seek new business partners among local engineering, procurement and construction companies and steel fabricators. During the second half of this year, GS Global will focus on establishing local networks, strengthening project pipeline management and stabilizing the branch’s operations. Beginning in 2027, it plans to expand project acquisition support and identify new business opportunities, with the goal of developing the Houston branch into a core hub for business development in the southern U.S. “Establishing the Houston branch is a strategic investment aimed at expanding our contact points with customers in the U.S. market and strengthening our practical sales capabilities,” a GS Global representative said. “We will identify diverse new opportunities, including project-based steel businesses, and establish a sustainable foundation for growth in North America.” With the opening of the Houston branch, GS Global now operates a global network of 23 overseas offices and entities across 16 countries. In the U.S., the company will enhance its market responsiveness through its Los Angeles subsidiary and the new Houston branch.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R Ashoka said the BJP and JD(S) had decided to boycott the Speaker election in protest against the ruling Congress "unconstitutionally" naming the new Speaker on its official letterhead. He accused the Congress of starting a new tradition in the country and the State by announcing the Speaker's name on its party letterhead, thereby undermining the sovereignty of the House and the rights of its elected representatives. He was referring to the Congress high command's letter to CM D. K. Shivakumar on August 3, which contained the names of 19 ministers to be inducted into his Cabinet. The letter also contained the names of the party's nominees for the post of Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Assembly, Chairperson, and Deputy Chairperson of the Council. Now, he has shared the first taste of that soundtrack, which arrives in full on August 21: a new song with the Blue Nile’s Paul Buchanan, “Pain Is the Heart of Love.” Listen to it below. Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma is Alex Giannascoli’s third collaboration with Schoenbrun—he also scored 2022’s We’re All Going to the World’s Fair and 2024’s I Saw the TV Glow. The new film follows a young director (Hannah Einbinder) who, in the process of rebooting a classic horror franchise, connects with the reclusive actress (Gillian Anderson) who played the series’ final girl. The tracklist also features songs from R.E.M., Sally Shapiro, Donna Lewis, and Okay Kaya. Elsewhere recently, Alex G co-produced Phoebe Bridgers’ third album Lost Weekend, wrapped up a North American tour, and released two new songs on his personal YouTube channel. Although Paul Buchanan has been scarce since releasing his 2012 solo album, Mid Air, he appeared on a Jessie Ware song in 2017 and a Quiet City track in 2021. title: Becky G’s Eclectic New Album ‘Baraja Bendita’ Is Here: Stream It Now - Billboard
content:
The Mexican-American artist bridged Becky G (the artist) and Rebbeca (her real name) in her new set. Becky G dropped her fifth studio album, Baraja Bendita, via RCA Records Friday (Aug. 14). In 17 tracks — including the previously released “EPA,” “Marathon” and “Patrona” — the Mexican-American singer bridges Becky G (the artist) and Rebbeca (her real name) as a musical symbol of duality, ownership and the freedom to exist fully without contradiction. “It’s about trusting myself enough to stop choosing between different parts of who I am,” she said in a statement. “For so long, people wanted to define me by one thing: one language, one sound, one version of myself. This album isn’t about becoming someone new. It’s about fully owning every part of who I’ve always been.” In contrast to her música mexicana-leaning projects Esquinas (2023) and Encuentros (2024), Becky proudly flaunts her 200% identity (100% American and 100% Mexican) powered by evolution and “baddie” energy. She seamlessly navigates from a kizomba and R&B fusion in “Chula,” to bachata in “Te va a doler,” merengue in “Mal Tiempo” and reggae in “Bandera Blanca.” She also delivers her signature reggaetón sound, as well as many club-ready bangers rooted in house and deep bass music. Written by Becky herself and not featuring any collaborations, the tracks on BB all find the artist allowing vulnerability and confidence, instinct and intention, to exist side by side. Baraja Bendita, which can loosely be translated as a “blessed deck of cards,” marks Becky’s fifth LP following Mala Santa (2019), Esquemas (2022), Esquinas (2023) and Encuentros (2024).
